newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian reporters should learn to shoot-police.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian reporters should learn to shoot-police.

text.p: Indonesian police have suggested that local journalists receive special training and shooting lessons to help them with the accuracy of their reporting, the official Antara news agency reported on Wednesday.

"If you need it, you can have shooting training with the riot police in order that you know that to shoot is not easy so that you are not always attacking the police if they make a mistake," the national police spokesman Brigadier-General Trimada Dani said.
Police in Jakarta have shot dead at least 70 criminals so far this year compared with 46 for the full year in 1996.

They say the victims, almost always repeat offenders, are shot while trying to resist arrest or escape from custody, and insist that police always fire warning shots in the air before aiming for the body.

Dani told the reporters during a social gathering on Tuesday that the shooting training would make them less cynical about reporting that the police were "bad shots" who aimed for the victims leg but shot them in the chest.
"Shooting's not easy. Not every one can firmly aim a weapon. People who for the first time hold a weapon tremble," he said.
